targets.name: ironshift
notes: Success rows and history are retained, unlike Graphile Worker.

targets.name: pg-boss
notes: Public work() owns claim and completion, so manual claim latency and Ironshift fencing are not directly comparable.
deleteAfterSeconds 0 disables age-based deletion for benchmark retention.
Handler batches of 10 are a product-specific sensitivity, not the controlled per-job contract.

targets.name: graphile-worker
notes: Successful jobs are deleted, so storage and WAL describe Graphile Worker's native retention semantics.
run() owns claiming; claim latency and Ironshift fence-token behavior are not directly comparable.

measurementNotes: Processing ends when every public task handler has completed successfully.
End-to-end spans the first enqueue call through the final successful handler completion.
Graceful worker shutdown and post-run telemetry are excluded from timed phases.
Framework-owned durable settlement may finish after the handler returns; exact completion is therefore handler-observed rather than a cross-product durable-settlement oracle.
This sensitivity run lets pg-boss invoke handlers in batches of 10; it is not a common per-job throughput ranking.
Equal-offered-load churn has one observation per target and is exploratory, not a confidence-backed ranking.
WAL and storage describe each product's declared native retention behavior and are not retention-normalized.
